title: Introduce prompt heterogeneity sensitivity latch and CI smoke guard
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Add a prompt-heterogeneity sensitivity latch to the eval harness and integrate a smoke CI hook that soft-fails when prompt-group behavioral dispersion exceeds calibrated thresholds. Adds telemetry and quarantine markers for failing prompt subsets.
description: Motivation: Some regression failures we see in CI are driven by increased variability across heterogeneous prompts (different intents/labels) rather than a global model degradation. This PR introduces a prompt heterogeneity sensitivity latch — a lightweight statistical guard that detects when the per-prompt-group dispersion (e.g., variance in composite quality score) exceeds an adaptive threshold and surfaces a soft-fail in CI with explanations and candidate quarantines. Goals: reduce noisy, non-actionable CI failures, provide clearer signals for prompt-set issues, and add tooling to quarantine subsets for focused debugging. What this changes: - New analysis module: eval/heterogeneity_latch.py implements bootstrap-calibrated dispersion thresholds, cohort weighting, and an explain API for top contributing prompts. - CI smoke hook: ci/hooks/heterogeneity_smokehook.py integrates the latch into the eval CI job; the hook reports structured reasons and can mark failing prompts with a quarantine tag in the eval artifact ledger. - Telemetry: metrics/tracing additions emit "eval.heterogeneity.score" and top-k prompt fingerprints for downstream dashboards. - Tests: unit and integration tests under tests/cover to validate sensitivity, bootstrap stability, and integration with existing eval reporter. - Docs/design: docs/decisions/heterogeneity_latch.md and a short how-to in docs/ci-ops/README.md. Backwards compatibility: default configuration keeps the latch in "monitor-only" mode (it annotates results but does not block merges) unless a repo-scale Linear flag is set. Checklist: - [x] Implement core latch algorithm with bootstrap calibration - [x] Add CI hook and wire into .github/workflows/eval-ci.yml (disabled by default in repo config) - [x] Add unit tests with synthetic prompt sets and a small real-world regression example - [x] Add telemetry tags and simple Grafana dashboard stub (not included in this PR) - [x] Update docs and add a troubleshooting section - [x] Add migration note for teams that enable strict gating in their config Known limitations and future work: We intentionally keep the latch conservative to avoid false positives on very small prompt cohorts; next work items include a cohort-size-aware smoothing policy and a human-in-the-loop quarantine approval flow. Related: ENG-4539 (design), PM-1180 (product ask), SUP-2231 (customer report about noisy CI failures). Links: design doc: docs/decisions/heterogeneity_latch.md; example run: ci/runs/heterogeneity-smoke/2026-02-18 (internal).

eval/heterogeneity_latch.py: 
def compute_latch(scores, groups, config):
    # bootstrap sample group-wise dispersion, compare to baseline quantile
    baseline = _load_baseline(config.baseline_path)
    disp = _group_dispersion(scores, groups)
    calibrated_q = _bootstrap_quantile(baseline, config.alpha)
    return {
        'score': disp,
        'threshold': calibrated_q,
        'explain': _top_contributors(scores, groups)
    }

  heterogeneity-smoke:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Run eval smoke with heterogeneity latch
        uses: actions/checkout@v3
        run: scripts/run_eval_smoke --with-heterogeneity-latch
